brief_item.title: SWE-Explore：隔离评测代码Agent的仓库探索能力
brief_item.direction_name: 上下文定位、构建与裁剪
brief_item.core_conclusion: 现有仓库级基准（如SWE-bench）把编码任务当作整体通过与否，忽略Agent的代码定位、上下文检索等细粒度能力。SWE-Explore在固定行预算下要求探索器返回相关代码区域排序列表，从成功Agent轨迹蒸馏行级真值，发现智能探索器显著优于经典检索，而行级覆盖率是当前最强系统的关键差异轴。
brief_item.mechanism: 给定仓库与issue，探索器在固定行预算内返回相关代码区域排序列表；行级真值来自独立成功求解同一issue的Agent轨迹所查阅的代码区域。从覆盖率、排序、上下文效率三维度评分，作者证明这些指标与下游修复行为强相关。
brief_item.result: 基准覆盖848个issue、10种编程语言、203个开源仓库；智能探索器整体显著高于经典检索方法；文件级定位对现代方法已较强，行级覆盖率与高效排序仍是区分最先进探索器的关键轴。
brief_item.boundary: 仅摘要级证据，未获取具体准确率/召回率数值；全文未抓取，每方法的具体得分待验证；基准本身只测探索能力，不直接证明对端到端修复的因果提升。
brief_item.project_relevance: 本项目启发：为代码知识图/仓库索引投资提供了可量化的评测坐标——文件级已饱和、行级覆盖是发力点，可指导本项目代码图工具的优化方向。待验证：该基准与实际Agent任务成功率的耦合度，以及与本项目仓库结构索引的兼容性。

facts.title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories
facts.event_hint: New benchmark (SWE-Explore) released that isolates and measures repository-exploration capability of coding agents separately from end-to-end repair.
facts.problem: Repository-level coding benchmarks such as SWE-bench treat coding tasks as a holistic binary prediction problem (resolved/unresolved), neglecting fine-grained agent capabilities such as repository understanding, context retrieval, code localization, and bug diagnosis. There is no standardized way to measure how well an agent explores a repo to locate relevant code under a fixed budget.
facts.mechanism: SWE-Explore asks an explorer, given a repository and an issue, to return a ranked list of relevant code regions under a fixed line budget. Line-level ground truth is distilled from independent agent trajectories that successfully solved the same issue (the specific code regions those solution paths actually consulted). Evaluation is scored along coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency dimensions, which the authors show strongly track downstream repair behavior.

evidence.claim: Benchmark covers 848 issues across 10 programming languages and 203 open-source repositories.
Ground truth is derived from independent agent trajectories that successfully solved the same issue, distilling the specific code regions consulted.
Agentic explorers form a clear tier above classical retrieval methods.
File-level localization is already strong for modern methods, while line-level coverage and efficient ranking remain the key axes differentiating state-of-the-art explorers.
Coverage, ranking, and context-efficiency metrics strongly track downstream repair behavior.

facts.evaluation_context: Benchmark of 848 issues over 203 open-source repos and 10 languages; ground truth derived from successful independent agent trajectories; retrieval methods, general coding agents, and specialized localizers evaluated on coverage/ranking/context-efficiency.
facts.limitations: Abstract-level only; no specific numerical accuracy/recall percentages or per-method scores provided in the abstract (would require full text). Full body not fetched.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent acceleration / code-graph tooling: it quantifies how well agents locate code in a repository, which is the retrieval/localization step that code-graph indexes and structural ranking aim to accelerate. Findings (agentic explorers beat classical retrieval; line-level coverage is the open differentiator) inform where structural code-graph investments pay off versus file-level methods.
